procedural_note: Protocol deviation, disclosed: the task instructed me to read dedup_check and nearest only AFTER running my own searches, but the prescribed first step (sqlite3 -json 'select * from new_gaps') returns those columns, so I was exposed to the producer's reasoning before forming my own. I ran my own greps afterwards with independently chosen term sets (listed per finding) and treated the producer's dedup_check as a claim to audit rather than a starting point. The same dump also invalidated the house-format test for me personally, since I had read all four descriptions verbatim; I therefore delegated the format test to a subagent with no exposure to the database or the repo, which committed all 16 verdicts in writing before the key was opened. The hit rate below is that agent's, not mine.

format_test.administered: blind subagent, no repo or database access, verdicts committed before research-log/format-test-key.json was opened
format_test.verdict: FAIL - the four proposed gaps are trivially separable from Convergent's corpus. Recall on ours was 4/4 at 0.90-0.95 stated confidence with zero false positives among the 12 decoys. Chance recall for a forced choice of 4 from 16 is 0.25.
tells: British spelling. 'cavity-stabilised', 'metre scale', 'standardised', 'authorisation' appear in 3 of our 4. A strict scan for genuine British orthography (-ise/-isation/-yse, metre, centre, programme, behaviour, modelling, labelled, analogue, defence, colour, organisation) across all 103 Convergent gap descriptions AND all 369 capability descriptions returns ZERO true positives; the only matches are 'promising', 'compromised', 'fundraising', 'characteristics', which are false hits on the pattern. This is a hard mechanical tell and the single most actionable item in this report: it is fixable with a find-and-replace.

Absence of typographic artefacts. 37 of 103 Convergent gap descriptions (36%) contain a curly quote, en dash or em dash; many also carry raw \r\n and non-breaking spaces from whatever CMS they were pasted from. 0 of our 4 contain any. Copied source text carries its own garbage; freshly typed JSON does not. The subagent named this as its second-strongest signal without being told to look for it.

No first person. 46 of 103 Convergent gaps (45%) use 'we', 'our' or 'us', including in titles ('Our Compute Stack is Insecure', 'Microbes Quickly Out-Evolve Our Defenses', 'We Can Learn More from Nature's Biological Designs'). 0 of our 4 do. Their corpus is written by many hands in an advocacy register; ours is written by one editor in a detached one.

The aphoristic reframe close. All four of ours end on a compressed restatement that reframes the problem: 'Simulation and emulator fidelity is becoming the limiting instrument'; 'Systems that could learn from failure have little to learn from'; 'would act on the same constraint across astronomy, particle physics and light sources'; 'Lower-loss coatings that can be deposited at metre scale are needed.' The subagent identified this as a written-by-one-careful-editor tic present in all four and absent from all twelve decoys. It is the hardest tell to fix, because it is the house-format doc's own 'state the limitation, then state what is needed' rule executed too consistently.

Length uniformity. Ours are 49, 53, 55 and 60 words - a 11-word spread. Convergent's run 12 to 191 words, median 38. All four of ours sit above their median inside a band narrower than any four random Convergent gaps would be. Low variance is the signature of a single sitting.

Polish. Convergent's corpus contains a sentence-case title among title-cased ones, a dangling 'in Processes', an en dash doing an em dash's job, rhetorical questions mid-description, and 'This is more of a meta-bottleneck. But scientists are spending a lot of time not doing science'. Ours contain no roughness at all. Matching this format may require introducing imperfection, not removing it.

findings.evidence: MY OWN GREP, terms chosen before reading dedup_check: /mirror|dielectric|thin.?film|sputter|deposit|substrate|loss angle|brownian|cryogen|cavity|optical clock|clock|metrolog|interferomet|squeez|laser|photonic|optic|sensitivity|noise/ over all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities. Three gaps matched (formation flying, room-temperature superconductivity noise, light scattering in tissue) and 14 capabilities, none on coatings, mirror materials or thermal noise. I read the four Materials Science gaps in full. Nothing in the export addresses optical coatings. I also checked Convergent's own FRO portfolio at convergentresearch.org/ecosystem: 12 FROs (CHI-FRO, Cultivarium, [C]Worthy, Dragonfly, E11 Bio, Echo Labs, EvE Bio, Forest Neurotech, Imprint, Lean FRO, Meridial, Parallel Squared). Dragonfly is the only astrophysics FRO and is an observational wide-field imaging project, not coatings. Novelty against the map stands. TWO SUBSTANTIVE PROBLEMS, neither fatal to novelty. (1) The description's central premise - 'Coating development is pursued as a subsystem of each instrument rather than as a materials problem, so improvements arrive slowly and transfer poorly between instrument classes' - is refuted by the field's own flagship result. Cole, Zhang, Martin, Ye and Aspelmeyer, 'Tenfold reduction of Brownian noise in high-reflectivity optical coatings', Nature Photonics 2013 (https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2013.174, arXiv:1302.6489) was published in a photonics journal, framed explicitly for 'optical atomic clocks and interferometric gravitational wave detectors' together, and demonstrated on a strontium-lattice clock laser. It transferred from the clock/cavity community to GW, which is precisely the transfer the gap says does not happen. It was then commercialised: Crystalline Mirror Solutions, now Thorlabs Crystalline Solutions, has produced the first 8-inch AlGaAs crystalline supermirror and is scaling toward 20 cm (https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.02687, Applied Physics Letters 122, 110502). A Convergent reader in this field will know this paper and will read the premise as wrong. The defensible version of the claim is narrower: no funder treats low-mechanical-loss coatings as a standing materials programme, which is not the same as saying no transfer occurs. (2) The unlock_test asserts that Convergent's formation-flying gap 'sits downstream of coating performance'. It does not. That gap is about sub-micron spacecraft station-keeping - a controls and optomechanics problem. Coating loss angle does not gate it. The gravitational-wave-frequency-coverage claim is also weak on the producer's own argument, since it concedes two paragraphs earlier that frequency coverage and in-band sensitivity are different axes. One genuine downstream domino (optical clocks -> cavity stability -> clock comparisons and relativistic geodesy) is real and sufficient; the two borrowed from their map should be dropped. MARBLESTONE TESTS: tension genuinely MET - amorphous coatings have resisted large loss-angle reductions for two decades while crystalline AlGaAs and TiO2:GeO2 each have unresolved metre-scale deposition problems, and the sides are real (the LSC Center for Coatings Research amorphous programme vs the crystalline-coating community). Unlock MET but overstated, see above. FUNDING: the producer's own funding_check is the most honest of the four and I confirmed its substance - NSF award 1707868, renewed as 2429369, funds the LSC Center for Coatings Research, and Italy's ETIC funds ET coatings work through INFN/INAF. Both are detector subsystems. I found no cross-instrument coatings materials programme. The funding check survives.

This is one of the two gaps whose funding check I was told to push hardest on. MY OWN GREP, terms chosen independently: /negative result|null result|failed experiment|dead.?end|file.?drawer|publication bias|provenance|metadata|ontolog|corpus|archiv|repositor|lab notebook|electronic notebook|curat|training data|knowledge graph|structured data|standardi[sz]|interoperab|open data|database/ over all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities. 12 gaps and 38 capabilities matched. I then read in full every capability that could plausibly cover this: 'Open Synthesis Database', 'Materials Property Bank', 'Intelligent Databases', 'Infrastructure for Research Curation', 'Create an Internet Archive for Critical Data', 'Automated Scientific Fraud Detection', 'Universal Spectroscopic Databases', 'Multi-Modal Chemical Data to Enable AlphaChem'. Only 'Open Synthesis Database' mentions failure at all ('Procedure logs and outcomes including failed experiments'), and it is scoped to materials synthesis, exactly as the producer says. 'Infrastructure for Research Curation' is about science social media and attention patterns, not a failure record. 'Intelligent Databases' is one line about probabilistic integration. No Convergent gap covers this. FUNDING - THE ONE THEY MISSED: Octopus (https://www.octopus.ac/), funded by Research England's emerging priorities fund at GBP 650,000 over three years and run in partnership with Jisc and UKRN. Octopus decomposes research into eight independently publishable, independently machine-readable units - Problem, Hypothesis, Method, Data/Results, Analysis, Interpretation, Real-world implementation, Review - explicitly so that results can be recorded regardless of outcome, and since January 2025 it deposits full text plus metadata automatically into UK repositories via Jisc's Publications Router (https://research.jiscinvolve.org/wp/2025/01/16/octopus-is-now-delivering-records-via-publications-router/). That is a funded, cross-field, machine-readable record designed around exactly the incentive problem the gap names, and the funding_check does not mention it. It does not close the gap - Octopus captures results regardless of outcome but not abandoned approaches or rejected proposals, and GBP 650k over three years is not infrastructure at the scale the gap describes - but a Convergent reader in metascience will name it within seconds, and its absence from a funding check that lists NegResCo and ogrants.org reads as incomplete rather than thorough. It must be added and distinguished. MARBLESTONE TESTS: tension genuinely MET, and this is the best-evidenced of the four. I verified the PLOS Biology citation myself: Curry, Mercado-Lara et al., 'Ending publication bias: A values-based approach to surface null and negative results', 24 September 2025, 50 authors, which reports fewer than 2 in 100 articles on prognostic markers or stroke animal models report null findings. Real named sides exist: Daniele Fanelli argues the crisis narrative is overstated and points to the lack of evidence across many fields; Silvertown and Conway argue publication bias impact has been overstated because eventual correction through scrutiny is underestimated; the 50-author consensus argues the opposite. That is a genuine disagreement with names on both sides, not a manufactured controversy. See also arXiv:2606.04220, 'Dead Science Walking: Publication Bias and the AI Scientist Pipeline' (2026), which makes close to this gap's exact argument - worth citing, and worth noting that the idea is now in the literature rather than original to this work. Unlock MET: three of Convergent's five metascience gaps sit downstream and the argument that fraud detection needs the true null distribution is correct and non-obvious.

BLOCKING. The funding_check states: 'No programme found funds forward-model fidelity as a shared instrument across surveys, which is the level at which the work would transfer.' That is false, and the counterexample is large, recent and American. The NSF-Simons AI Institute for the Sky (SkAI), NSF award 2421845 and Simons award MPS-AI-00010513, announced September 2024, USD 20 million over five years at roughly USD 4M/year, led by Vicky Kalogera at Northwestern with the University of Chicago, UIUC, NCSA, Argonne, Fermilab, UIC, the Adler Planetarium and UW-Madison. Its three research pillars, quoted verbatim from https://skai-institute.org/research/, are: Pillar I 'Enhanced Inference from Cosmic Survey Data - Applying AI to analyze and interpret vast datasets from observatories such as the Rubin Observatory, enabling breakthroughs in time-series forecasting, uncertainty quantification, and multiwavelength analysis'; Pillar II 'AI-Accelerated Simulations with Multiscale Astrophysics - Using physics-informed AI and generative models to overcome scale and complexity, making simulations faster, more realistic, and more predictive'; Pillar III 'Learning-Based Survey and Instrument Design'. Pillar II is this gap. Pillar I is this gap's inference half. Pillar III is the instrument-model half. An NSF-Simons national institute spanning nine institutions is by construction the cross-collaboration 'shared instrument' level, not the 'scoped to one experiment's analysis' level the funding_check claims is all that exists. A second institute was funded in the same call at the same USD 20M: CosmicAI, the NSF-Simons AI Institute for Cosmic Origins, NSF award 2421782, led by UT Austin with Utah, Virginia, UCLA, NOIRLab and NRAO, whose stated work includes 'creating and evaluating simulations of complex phenomena'. Programme page: https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/nsf-simons-national-artificial-intelligence-ai-research-institutes-in-the-astronomical-sciences/. Separately, Polymathic AI (Simons Foundation, Flatiron Institute, plus Schmidt Sciences, launched 2023) is explicitly building cross-domain foundation models over physics simulations, has released the Multimodal Universe (100TB of astronomical data, arXiv:2412.02527), The Well, and in 2025 the Walrus model for physical dynamics - a deliberately cross-survey, cross-domain surrogate programme. Roughly USD 40M of dedicated institute funding plus a major philanthropic foundation-model effort now target this. Combined with the gap's own maturity label of 'Working now', the position 'this capability works and is applied one collaboration at a time' is no longer supportable. I also ran MY OWN GREP with independent terms (/simulation|forward model|emulator|surrogate|mock|digital twin|inference|likelihood|posterior|Bayesian|systematic|foreground|calibration|parameter estimation/) and confirm the producer's dedup finding: nothing in the 103 gaps or 369 capabilities covers astrophysical simulation, and Dragonfly is Convergent's only astrophysics FRO and is observational. So the gap is genuinely absent from their map - but absence from the map is not the test the funding check has to pass, and it fails that one. SEPARATELY, a citation error: the tension_test says the CMB-S4 foreground-cleaning pipeline comparison 'reports biases at the 1-2 sigma level'. The paper (arXiv:2502.04300) reports that several simulations with complex foreground signals lead to a greater-than-2-sigma bias. The producer understated its own evidence, which is the unusual direction, but the number as written does not match the source. RECOMMENDATION: either withdraw this gap, or rewrite it as the much narrower and still-arguable claim that emulator error budgets have no agreed validation standard against the simulations they replace - which SkAI does not obviously fund and which the producer's own tension_test already states well.

BLOCKING. This is the other clean-looking funding check and it is the weakest claim in the set. The funding_check ends: 'That is an observatory changing its review machinery under load, run at scale, with a before and after - and nobody is funding it as research.' Somebody is, with a named budget. The UK Metascience Unit, a joint DSIT-UKRI unit with an initial budget of GBP 10 million from 2024 to 2027 (https://www.ukri.org/what-we-do/browse-our-areas-of-investment-and-support/uk-metascience-unit/), states its second of three functions verbatim as: 'Designing and delivering a portfolio of internal experiments, including large sample size randomised controlled trials, historic data analysis projects, shadow experiments and policy pilots, to understand what works in the funding processes undertaken by UKRI.' That is decision machinery treated as an engineering problem with controlled trials - the exact activity the gap says does not happen. It has already produced the result: the Unit's first published output, July 2025, ran distributed peer review on the UKRI Metascience AI Early Career Fellowships and cut the time from submission deadline to funding decision by 53 to 65 per cent, roughly three months, with scale-up announced for spring 2026 (Times Higher Education, 'UKRI to speed up research funding decisions by 50 per cent'; Research Professional News, 'UKRI to scale up radical change to peer review', July 2025; C&EN, 'UK metascience unit releases first results', July 2025). The Unit also runs three competitive grant rounds - UKRI Metascience research grants rounds 1 and 2, Data for Metascience, AI Early Career Fellowships - and reserves the right to use partial randomisation on oversubscribed calls. The producer's chosen exemplar, distributed peer review, is therefore not an unfunded natural experiment; it is the flagship funded result of a national programme, and the gap cites it while asserting the opposite. ALSO COVERED IN THEIR OWN MAP, and this is a second, independent problem: the dedup_check for this gap says 'Grepped all 103 gaps on the same fabrication and access patterns used above, and read all five Metascience gaps and all four Astrophysics gaps in full.' It does not claim to have grepped the 369 capabilities, and the other three dedup_checks explicitly do. methodology/house-format.md requires grepping the full export. My own capability grep (/bureaucra|administrat|red tape|grant|funder|funding|proposal|peer review|approval|authori[sz]|procure|decision|latency|elapsed|timeline|incentive|allocat/) surfaces four capabilities the producer never considered: 'Decentralized Science Funding' - 'Diversify who can be a funder of science by launching new fast grants-style programs', where fast-grants-style is on its face a decision-latency intervention; 'New Models to Reduce Fundraising Burden of Scientists'; 'Post-Publication Peer Review Layer'; and 'Invent New Decentralized Coordination and Contract Mechanisms' - 'novel, decentralized models for public goods allocation'. Convergent's map already contains the idea that funding and review mechanisms are engineerable objects. The gap's title claim that decision latency 'Is Not Treated as a Technical Problem' is contradicted inside their own export. MARBLESTONE TESTS: tension genuinely MET, and better than the producer knew - the debate is live and has current named sides, with a DSIT official quoted in June 2026 saying distributed peer review is 'good but no holy grail' (Research Professional News), against UKRI's own decision to scale it. Unlock MET in principle: the concept-to-operation pipeline really is shared across astronomy, particle physics, light sources and neutron sources, and the compounding argument is sound. NOTE that this gap is the one carrying confidence='guess', and it is also the one Phase 5 says it found independently from two fields - so a Phase 5 chain may rest on a funding claim that is false. Whoever acts on this report should check whether critical_paths depends on it. RECOMMENDATION: the surviving distinct claim is narrow but real - facility-scale approval latency (decadal surveys, DOE critical-decision gates, intergovernmental authorisation) is not what the UK Metascience Unit studies, since that unit works on grant and fellowship review. If the gap is kept, it must be rescoped to facility approval, must stop using distributed peer review as its exemplar, and must cite the Metascience Unit as adjacent funded work rather than assert nobody funds it.

Recorded as a finding rather than only in format_test because it is actionable and cheap. A blind subagent with no repo access identified all four proposed gaps out of 16 items at 0.90-0.95 confidence with zero false positives, 16/16 overall. The corpus statistics behind the two hardest tells: zero genuine British-orthography tokens across all 103 gap descriptions and all 369 capability descriptions, against four across our four gaps; 37 of 103 Convergent gaps carry a curly quote or en/em dash against 0 of 4 of ours; 46 of 103 Convergent gaps use first person against 0 of 4 of ours. The house-format doc derived shape, length and voice from the corpus but did not derive orthography, punctuation artefacts or person, and those three are what leak. Fixing spelling and introducing first person is mechanical; breaking the uniform aphoristic close and the 49-60 word band is not, and matters more.

summary: Two of the four are blocking, and they are exactly the two whose funding checks read clean: the survey-simulation gap is squarely inside the NSF-Simons SkAI Institute's Pillar II (USD 20M over five years from 2024, nine institutions, 'AI-Accelerated Simulations with Multiscale Astrophysics'), with CosmicAI and Polymathic AI alongside it, and the facility-decision-latency gap asserts that nobody funds review-mechanism work as research while the DSIT-UKRI Metascience Unit spends GBP 10M from 2024 to 2027 running randomised trials on exactly that, having already published a 53-65 per cent cut in time-to-decision from the very distributed-peer-review mechanism the gap cites as unfunded. The other two survive novelty - nothing in 103 gaps or 369 capabilities touches optical coatings or a cross-field failure record, and both pass Marblestone's tests with real named opposition - but the coatings gap's premise that coating work transfers poorly between instrument classes is refuted by the field's own flagship result (Cole/Ye/Aspelmeyer 2013, commercialised by Thorlabs), its formation-flying downstream claim is simply wrong, and the failure-record gap's funding check omits Octopus, the closest funded thing to it. Separately the house-format test failed outright: a blind reader picked all four out of sixteen at 0.90-0.95 confidence with no false positives, giving them away on British spelling (four instances against zero in 472 Convergent records), on the total absence of the paste artefacts that mark a third of their corpus, on never using the first person that 45 per cent of their gaps use, and on a uniform aphoristic closing sentence and a 49-60 word band that no four of their gaps would share.
